description: Gold-standard bounded-context labelling of the synthetic e-commerce monolith. Each source module is mapped to the microservice/domain it *should* belong to after decomposition. This is the reference partition the proposed decomposition is scored against (ARI, F1, etc.).
realism_notes: discovery (catalogue browse), rating (pricing) and basket (cart) are named for their mechanism rather than their domain, so a decomposition has to classify them from behaviour rather than filename. logistics spans two contexts: it is labelled Orders because it belongs to the order lifecycle, but its code manipulates warehouse stock, so a content-based classifier can reasonably place it under Inventory. Both cases are why mock-mode ARI lands below 1.0. Labels were not adjusted to raise the score.

Platform.description: Cross-cutting configuration, persistence and shared entities. In a real migration this becomes a shared library or is duplicated per service, not a runtime microservice.

Users/Auth.description: Identity: registration, login/session issuance and user profiles.

Catalog.description: Product catalogue browsing and price computation.

Orders.description: Cart and checkout orchestration — the first service extracted via strangler fig.
